_comment: WC2026 ROUND OF 16, 2026-07-04 (first R16 tie modelled). KNOCKOUT: no draw -- level after 90' -> extra time -> penalties, so the deliverable is who ADVANCES. Routes: Canada (co-HOST) finished 2nd in Group B (1-1 Bosnia, 6-0 Qatar, 1-2 Switzerland; 4 pts, GF 8 GA 3, rating 75) -- ATTACKING (8 goals, thumped Qatar 6-0) but beatable (lost to Switzerland, not airtight) -- then won R32 1-0 vs South Africa (clean sheet, settled in 90'). Morocco finished 2nd in Group C (1-1 Brazil, 1-0 Scotland, 4-2 Haiti; 7 pts, GF 6 GA 3, rating 83) -- organized, defensively solid (HELD BRAZIL 1-1), and then pulled the round's big upset, ELIMINATING the Netherlands on penalties (1-1) in the R32. Morocco arrive in red-hot form and are the higher-rated side. Class gap ~8 (83 vs 75) -> MOROCCO the favourite by class AND form. BUT Canada is the nominal home side and a co-host: venue for this R16 tie is NOT confirmed in the data (KO_VENUE 'various'); IF played in Canada (Toronto/Vancouver) the home edge is real, so a MODEST home nudge is applied (base_home 1.28) -- flagged as venue-dependent, kept small in case it is a neutral US venue. Net: Morocco the clear-ish favourite, Canada a live home underdog that can score. KNOCKOUT CAUTION: both are competent (NOT a leaky-underdog shut-out setup), so a moderate total (~2.6) and a genuine BTTS ~53% is honest here -- this is not the over-lean-BTTS trap (neither side is a leaky minnow); but keep the draw/ET tail respected (close tie). A competitive, near-even R16 tie with elevated extra-time/penalty risk. Home = Canada (nominal; possible real home). Cards not modelled (referee TBD).

_postmatch.verdict: Right side, wrong texture -- and TWO corrections fall out. Morocco advanced as the 57.2% pick (✅ on the deliverable), but (1) the MARGIN blew past the near-even read: I made this a LOW-confidence, ~57/43 tie; Morocco won 3-0, playing like the clear favourite their form implied (they had just held Brazil 1-1 and eliminated the Netherlands). I UNDER-weighted red-hot Morocco and over-credited Canada's home edge -- the market had Morocco only 40.6% too, so it is partly variance, but a 3-0 says Morocco was the stronger side by more than I priced. (2) The BTTS-Yes lean (53%) was WRONG AGAIN -- Canada was shut out. This is the THIRD straight time I leaned both-score on a 'favourite vs an attacking-looking underdog' tie and the favourite kept a clean sheet: USA 2-0 Bosnia, Switzerland 2-0 Algeria, now Morocco 3-0 Canada. The BTTS bias is no longer small-n noise; it is a systematic error and is corrected below.
_postmatch.lesson: BTTS RULE UPGRADE (see results_log standing note, now quantified): in a knockout with ANY clear-ish favourite, the underdog gets SHUT OUT far more often than group-calibrated lambdas imply -- lean BTTS-NO and lift the favourite's clean sheet by trimming the UNDERDOG's lambda ~15-20% on top of base calibration. Reserve BTTS-Yes for GENUINELY EVEN ties (advancement ~50/50) between two attacking sides. Three-for-three now (USA, Switzerland, Canada all shut out). Secondary lesson: don't over-discount a favourite in RED-HOT knockout form (Morocco had just beaten Brazil-level opposition) toward a coin-flip just because the underdog is a home co-host; weight recent knockout form, not only rating + venue. Advancement side was right (57% -> Morocco through); the corrections are to margin (rate in-form Morocco higher) and texture (BTTS down).
